back: The function initiating the function call is the caller, and the function being called (executed) is the callee. A function call is also sometimes called an invocation, with the caller invoking the callee.
front: What is the difference between a function caller and a function callee?
source_prefix: here you left off.C++ programs can work the same way (and borrow some of the same nomenclature). A program will be executing statements sequentially inside one function when it encounters a function call. A function call tells the CPU to interrupt the current function and execute another function. The CPU essentially “puts a bookmark” at the current point of execution, executes the function named in the function call, and then returns to the point it bookmarked and resumes execution.Nomenclature
